_doc: Parked type reconstructions. Existing 1835 stands and generic 1904 C02 remain separate. The additional Brougham follows an evidenced 1893 catalogue design; its individual presence, owner and stop are reconstructed. L-parked-vehicles-2979; L-covered-wagons-2980; L-brougham-parked-2794.

wagon_w01.basis: Original reconstructed farm-box geometry follows the existing1835 yard envelope, with individual boards, iron hardware and original procedural finish. No exact manufacturer/model is established.

carriage_c02.basis: Original enclosed-carriage reconstruction for1904, with a dark cabin, painted running gear and glazed openings. It is not identified as a particular maker, catalog model or person's carriage.

covered_w01_western_blue.basis: Original empty covered-wagon reconstruction with faded blue body and oxide running gear, open canvas ends, bows, restrained seams/folds and a laid-by ox yoke. The original record ID and exact coordinates retain its seeded finish family and canvas aging. Canvas construction, color, wear and bows are reconstructed; no manufacturer, historical owner or load is identified. Source-owned donor bench/footboard were omitted; occupied, driver, hitch, collision, riding and boarding interfaces are unsupported.

covered_w01_wolfpoint_oak.basis: Original empty covered-wagon reconstruction with aged oak body and dark oak running gear, open canvas ends, bows, restrained seams/folds and a laid-by ox yoke. The original record ID and exact coordinates retain its seeded finish family and canvas aging. Canvas construction, color, wear and bows are reconstructed; no manufacturer, historical owner or load is identified. Source-owned donor bench/footboard were omitted; occupied, driver, hitch, collision, riding and boarding interfaces are unsupported.

studebaker_brougham_1893.basis: Original empty, unhitched Brougham reconstruction guided by Studebaker's 1893 catalogue illustration, leaf 0095. The shaped roof, curved door, separate footplates, fine step supports and dark rear quarters follow the depicted design. Metric dimensions, unseen construction, paint and surface materials, and this particular vehicle's presence, ownership and stop in 1904 are reconstructed. The catalogue does not identify the dark rear surface as glass or a curtain. Photographic refinement continues.

design_reference.value: Studebaker Brothers Manufacturing Company — Brougham, 1893 catalogue
design_reference.note: The 1893 catalogue documents this maker and carriage type before the scene date. It does not document this reconstructed individual vehicle, its presence in Chicago or its ownership.

1835.note: A refined unhitched farm-box type replaces the previous vehicle at the same reconstructed stand and bearing. Maker, owner, cargo and finish are unidentified. The existing yard source supports the kind of setting, not this exact wagon.

1904.name: Enclosed town carriage
1904.note: A reconstructed temporary curbside stop in the1904 carriageway, clear of the sidewalk and crossing. Its location does not identify the owner or imply use by the Glessner household. Empty and unhitched; doors remain closed and boarding is not enabled.

1904.name: Brougham — after Studebaker’s 1893 catalogue
1904.location: Prairie Avenue carriageway south of Eighteenth Street
1904.note: Reconstructed empty, unhitched parked individual using the 1893 catalogue design reference. The catalogue establishes the maker/type before 1904; neither this particular vehicle, its owner, a household connection nor this curbside stop is documented. Generic C02 remains a separate unidentified reconstruction at its existing stand. Closed doors, no occupant, horse, boarding, traffic or driving.
